name: GitCat v1.5.0
body:
A commit's diff can open in a window of its own, and the signature badge now reports what git actually says instead of guessing. Partial clones work, the plugin sandbox is a real sandbox, and GitCat has changed colour.

## A diff in a window of its own

The expanded diff used to be a near-fullscreen overlay stranded in the window that opened it. It now has a **pop out** button that moves it into a separate, diff-only GitCat window — no sidebar, no branches, no graph, and not a second copy of the repository. The new window boots straight into that commit's diff, already expanded, skipping the repo-wide graph load entirely.

**Settings ▸ General ▸ Open diffs in** chooses what the expand icon does by default. The modal stays the default, and the pop-out button is there either way.

## Commit signatures come from git now

Real repositories always showed "Unsigned", and design mode made good-or-bad up from the row number — while the documentation advertised GPG status anyway. GitCat now asks git itself and reports what it answers: **good**, **untrusted**, **expired**, **bad**, **unverified**, or none. Only the selected commit is checked, debounced and with a timeout, and it never blocks the diff.

Two distinctions it is careful about. "Cannot check" is never shown as **bad** — a public key you do not have is not a forged commit — and the reason is shown instead. An ssh-signed commit with no `allowedSignersFile` configured reads as **unverified** for the same reason.

## Partial clones

In a `--filter=blob:none` clone every diff failed with `object not found`, and preview, blame and file history went with it, because libgit2 cannot lazily fetch from a promisor remote. GitCat now notices which blobs are missing and fetches them in one git call, mirroring what git's own lazy fetch does. An ordinary repository pays one cached `stat` and nothing else.

Two costs worth knowing: **blame** has to walk history to batch-fetch every version of the file, which on a repository the size of CPython takes a few seconds, and comparing two distant commits may download a lot of blobs. Offline, you get a translated explanation rather than the raw git error.

## Plugins

- **The `git()` sandbox is now a sandbox.** It filtered a few global options and let the rest through — enough to run arbitrary programs via `alias.*='!sh…'`, `core.fsmonitor`, `core.hooksPath`, `core.sshCommand`, `--upload-pack`, `rebase -x` or `--ext-diff`, to read and write outside the repository through `--output`, `format-patch --signature-file` and `--no-index`, and to delete the refs Undo recovers from. There is a subcommand allowlist now, and option filtering that understands abbreviations, `--opt=value`, `-Xvalue` and `--`. Every escape vector has a test.
- **`{files}` has a definition.** The manifest suggested it and it had no possible value. In a `commit` command it is the selected commit's changed paths, not capped at the detail pane's 40 files; in the new **`staged`** context it is the staged paths, read fresh at each run, so a pre-commit lint works with nothing selected. An empty staged set is refused rather than letting `prettier --write {files}` reformat the whole project.
- **Placeholders work on Windows.** Values were POSIX single-quoted, which `cmd` ignores, and Rust's argv quoting mangled every `"` in a template. Both are fixed and verified against real `cmd.exe`. Values containing shell metacharacters are still refused, as before.
- **A fifth example plugin.** `staged-review` exercises panels, all four widget types, a Tama skin and the new `staged` context.

## Warm amber

The indigo accent on cool blue-grey is now an amber accent — Tama's own fur family — on warm greys, in the app and on the docs site. Every text colour clears AA contrast in both themes and the graph's lane colours are unchanged. Warning moves to mustard so it stops reading as the accent, and light-theme success was under 4.5:1 on white and now is not.

## Also

- **The graph no longer blanks after an Undo.** A reload swapped in empty rows before any data came back, leaving roughly two seconds of empty canvas on a large repository. The old rows now stay painted, dimmed and click-proof, until the new stream's first batch arrives.
- **A second window's graph could stay blank forever.** Opening a window while another was running could paint the first frame before the backend replied; `draw()` threw on the null graph, and because the redraw loop reschedules itself on its last line, it never ran again. Clicking still worked, which is what made it confusing.
- **`gitcat --version` no longer opens an empty window.** `--version` and `--help` print and exit, an unknown option is an error with exit code 2, and `gitcat -- <path>` opens a path that starts with a dash. On Windows the output reaches the terminal despite the GUI subsystem.
- **Shortcut hints are spelled per platform.** Windows and Linux were shown macOS glyphs — `⌘Z` in the Reset HEAD dialog, `⌘K` in the search box, and tooltips. The labels now come from the same table as the real bindings, so they cannot drift from them.
- **"Undo with stash?" could never appear.** The frontend matched an English phrase against what was by then a translation key, so the prompt was unreachable — and English-only back when it had worked. The same bug in the merge-tool hint is fixed too.
- **The docs no longer overclaim the Safety Manager.** README, docs and in-app text all said every mutation snapshots "refs, index, worktree and stash". It pins HEAD and the local branch tips; uncommitted work is covered only by specific discard backups. Every one of those claims now says that, in all three languages.
- **Linux x86_64: the AppImage starts in a sandbox again.** v1.4.0's did not. Its repack corrected `AppRun.wrapped` and then stored all 58 of its directories at `0700`, including the filesystem root — so the failure moved up a level instead of going away, and the app still could not start wherever the running user did not own the files. The pipeline now reads the permissions the image really carries rather than an extracted copy's, and repacks both architectures.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do for most people. Existing repositories, settings and plugins carry over, and the amber theme applies itself.

Two things if you write or install plugins. **A plugin whose command ids are malformed or duplicated is now rejected at install**, where it used to load with one command silently shadowing the other; if a third-party plugin stops installing, the error names the id. And sandboxed `git()` calls now run with hooks disabled — so a plugin commit skips husky and Gerrit Change-Id — while a handler that does not declare `mutates` can no longer mutate at all. Both are documented in `docs/plugins.md`, and the shipped examples are unaffected.

Linux users on the x86_64 AppImage should take this release: v1.4.0's does not start in a sandbox.

name: GitCat v1.4.0
body:
Plugins get a catalogue you can browse from inside GitCat, and can now teach the diff view new languages. On Linux x86_64, the AppImage starts in places the last one could not.

## Browse for plugins without leaving the app

**Tools ▸ Plugins…** has a new **Browse** tab. It reads the [gitcat-plugins](https://github.com/zangjiucheng/gitcat-plugins) community index — official entries and community ones — and can fetch a listed plugin for you, so finding one no longer means hunting down a `plugin.json` by hand.

Installing from it is the ordinary install with the file-picking done for you, not one click that runs something. GitCat downloads the plugin's files, and then shows you **exactly what it runs** — every command, every hook and its event, anything that writes to your repository — before anything is installed. A listed plugin gets no more trust than one you downloaded yourself: the index says where a plugin is, never that anyone audited it.

## Plugins can teach the diff view a language

A plugin can now declare syntax-highlighting grammars, so a language GitCat does not highlight itself can be added by a plugin rather than by waiting for GitCat to support it.

## The terminal

The drawer now closes when its shell exits, instead of leaving an empty terminal behind. On Windows, its shell picker can switch between installed WSL distributions.

## Linux: the AppImage starts where it used to refuse

If v1.3.2's x86_64 AppImage would not launch for you, this is why. It shipped one file — `AppRun.wrapped`, which `AppRun` execs on the way in — without execute permission for anyone but its owner. That is invisible when you run it as yourself, and fatal everywhere else: under a sandbox like firejail, under `APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN` on machines without FUSE, and under tools that extract and re-own the files.

The release pipeline now checks every AppImage it builds and repacks and re-signs the x86_64 one when it needs it. The aarch64 AppImage was never affected.

## Also

- **The licence is detectable again.** `LICENSE` had the project's own applied-GPL notice ahead of the licence text, so GitHub reported no licence at all. It is now the verbatim GPL-3.0; the notice moved to the README.
- **Safety Manager on WSL** — backup refs are created through the distribution's own git (#193).
- **The Luau sandbox docs were wrong** about `pcall`. They listed it among the functions available to a handler, but the sandbox strips `pcall` and `xpcall`, so a handler that followed the docs hit a nil at runtime. Thanks @SAY-5 for the fix.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. Existing repositories, settings and plugins carry over.

name: GitCat v1.3.2
body:
A maintenance release. Most of what is in it was broken in ways that were hard to see: a second window quietly undoing the first one's work, a terminal that swallowed the shell's own keys, a column that had been half missing at the default width for some time.

## If you use two windows

Every GitCat window is a separate process, and the two on-disk lists — your tracked repositories and your installed plugins — were guarded by a lock that only works *within* one process. So enabling a plugin in one window while adding a repository in another could silently drop one of the two changes. Whichever window saved second won, and nothing said so.

That lock is now taken from the operating system, so it holds across windows. Nothing was ever corrupted by this — the file on disk was always whole, just occasionally the wrong one of two.

## If your repositories live in WSL

Opening one failed outright with *"repository path is not owned by current user"*. GitCat has always handled that refusal by adding the path to git's `safe.directory` and trying again, but on Windows it ran that write from inside the repository's own folder — and a Windows process cannot stand in a `\\wsl.localhost\` path. The write never happened, so the retry hit the same wall.

Reported and confirmed fixed by the person who hit it.

## The built-in terminal

It had no key handling at all, which meant two things: every GitCat shortcut competed with the shell, and once your cursor was in the terminal there was no way back to the app without the mouse.

**Ctrl+K** now reaches readline's kill-line instead of opening the command palette, and the same goes for every other chord the shell wants. **Shift+Escape** returns focus to the graph, leaving the drawer open — Escape stays the shell's, because vim and readline both need it. The drawer shows the shortcut in its header.

## The command palette

Searching **check update** put Settings first, because Settings' description happens to contain both words and it sits higher in the list. Results are now ranked by their *title*, so the thing you named comes first.

**⌥1–9** jumps straight to a result; the numbers are on the rows.

And with the palette open, **⌘1** used to move focus to the graph behind it, leaving a dialog on screen you could no longer type into. The palette now holds the keyboard while it is up.

## Two things you could see

- **Author and Committer.** A long email address forced each column wider than the space it had, and the overflow was hidden rather than wrapped — so the Committer column was **half missing at the default panel width** and entirely gone below about 230px. Addresses wrap now, and the pair stacks when the panel is too narrow for two readable columns.
- **The search box** in the title bar wrapped onto two lines from about a 1000px window down, making it taller than the bar it sits in. It stays on one line and shortens instead.

## Faster

- **Every short git command was paying a flat 30 ms wait.** GitCat checks whether a subprocess has finished on a timer, and the first check always came too early, so a `git config` that took 8 ms still cost 30. It now checks quickly at first and backs off. That is about 13 ms back per command — roughly 100 ms off opening Settings, which reads eight of them in a row.
- **Loading a widely-branched repository** does less work on the thread that draws the window: each batch of graph rows is now prepared on the background thread that produced it. On a repository with hundreds of simultaneous branches that is about 2.8 ms per batch, and such a repository hits it on nearly every batch.

## Plugins

Editing a plugin's `plugin.json` used to mean removing and reinstalling it — its Luau script was already re-read on every run, but the manifest was not. There is an **Update** button next to Remove; it re-reads the manifest from the folder the plugin was installed from.

If you had disabled the plugin, it stays disabled. The file's own `enabled` value is deliberately ignored, because a manifest that omits it defaults to on, and that would switch a plugin you turned off back on behind your back.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. Repositories, settings and plugins carry over.

---

name: GitCat v1.3.1
body:
Everything in GitCat can now be reached from the keyboard, you can compare two commits directly on the graph, and the app finally shows you what a plugin runs before you install it.

## The keyboard

GitCat had shortcuts; it did not have a keymap. Around forty operations had no keyboard path at all, and the ones that existed disagreed with each other — ⌘⇧Z undid instead of redoing, Escape closed two dialogs at once, a commit message could be lost by pressing it.

There is a single binding table now, and the app is driven from it. Press **⌘1 / ⌘2 / ⌘3** to move between the graph, the sidebar and the detail panel; the pane you are in wears a ring so you can see where a keystroke will land.

In the working tree, **s** and **u** stage and unstage the selected file, **S** and **U** do all of them, **d** discards, and **⌘↵** commits. On the graph, **x** opens the same actions menu the right mouse button does, the arrow keys move the selection (they used to only scroll, leaving the cursor behind), and **Home** / **End** jump to the ends. In the sidebar, **f** focuses the filter, **c** checks out, **x** opens the row's menu. **t** cycles the detail panel's tabs.

Press **?** for the full list. That overlay is generated from the binding table rather than written by hand, so it cannot drift from what the keys actually do — the old one already had.

## Compare two commits

Select a commit, right-click another, and choose **Compare with…**. A popover tells you how many commits sit between the two, what the net change is, and lists the chain; **View diff…** opens the whole per-file diff.

"Lines changed" is the net delta between the two points, not the sum of everything that happened in between — a line edited three times and put back counts as zero, which is what "what is different between these two commits" usually means.

## Plugins: you can see what they do

GitCat's plugin model has always been blunt about itself — there is no sandbox, and a plugin's `run` string is shell text executed on your machine. The documentation asked you to install only plugins you would run yourself. The app never showed you the commands.

It does now. Choosing a `plugin.json` no longer installs it: GitCat validates the manifest and shows you every command's command line verbatim, every hook and the event it fires on, anything that writes to your repository, and the folder it loads from. Nothing is installed until you agree. The same view is in the Plugins panel for anything already installed, so you can check later what you agreed to.

Two holes closed alongside it:

- **Disabling a plugin now actually stops it.** Disabling stopped a plugin's hooks but not its commands — including ones that write to your repository — because the executor never checked the flag.
- **A misspelled manifest key is now rejected** instead of silently ignored. A `mutates` typed as `mutatez` used to produce a command that quietly took no safety snapshot.

## Fixes

- The detail panel no longer flashes on every refresh, and keeps the file you were reading, the message you had expanded and the folders you had collapsed. Switching commits crossfades in place instead of briefly drawing the new commit below the old one.
- Dialogs can no longer be cut off by a short window. Twenty-one of them could be — including ones that looked safe, because capping the body's height still left the header and footer to push past the edge.
- The highlight marking a cherry-picked or rebased commit got its corners back.

## Faster

The graph truncated long text by removing one character and measuring again, in a loop — about 216 measurements per row, every frame, on a repository with long commit subjects. It bisects now: roughly five times quicker on a frame that triggers it. Font strings and the sha width are computed once per frame rather than once per row, and four modal islands load on first open rather than at boot.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. Existing repositories, settings and plugins carry over.

name: GitCat v1.3.0
body:
The detail panel can move to the bottom of the window and gained tabs, file and folder rows got right-click menus, and plugins can now declare which GitCat they need and receive the selected file.

## The detail panel, along the bottom

There is a placement setting now, and it sticks. Choose "bottom" and the panel becomes a full-width row under the graph instead of a right-hand column, resized by dragging its top edge.

Either way it has tabs: Commit and Changes for a commit, Commit, Changes and Stash for the working tree. The expanded-diff splitter follows the placement rather than staying vertical.

## Right-click menus

File rows, folder rows and the repository chip in the top bar all carry a context menu, with the actions that surface already shows as buttons. It also adds "Show in Finder/Explorer/file manager" and opening a folder directly.

Both of those go through GitCat's own backend rather than the webview's file opener. The permissive path would have meant granting the webview the right to ask the OS to open any path at all, and GitCat runs third-party plugin code in that webview.

## For plugin authors

**`minGitcatVersion`** lets a manifest declare the oldest GitCat that can run it, and an older copy refuses the install with a message naming both versions. This matters because an unrecognized placeholder token expands to the empty string, so a plugin written against a newer GitCat did not fail loudly on an older one: a `run` of `rm {file}` quietly became `rm`. Declaring the floor turns that into a refusal at the one moment someone is there to read it.

Older releases ignore the field, so it protects hosts from 1.3.0 on rather than retroactively.

**`{file}` is now filled in** for a command declaring `"context": "file"`, taken from whichever view is open: the working tree's selection when Uncommitted changes is showing, the commit's otherwise. With nothing selected the command is refused rather than run with an empty path, since an empty token would turn `rm -rf {repo}/{file}` into `rm -rf` on the repository itself.

## Windows

The terminal opens in the repository instead of `C:\Windows`.

`git bisect run` now hands your test command to `cmd.exe` unmangled. Previously the quoting was rewritten on the way through, so a command that never actually ran was scored as BAD and the bisect converged on the wrong first-bad commit, with nothing to indicate it had gone wrong.

The Rust test suite also compiles and runs on Windows for the first time, which is what made the two fixes above findable.

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. Existing repositories, settings and plugins carry over.

name: GitCat v1.2.0
body:
GitCat 1.2.0 is about seeing things clearly: a third language, diffs for files that aren't text, and a graph that responds the way you expect when you click it. Every operation that touches history still snapshots first, so Undo (⌘Z) is always one keystroke away.

## Korean (한국어)

The whole interface now runs in Korean, joining English and Simplified Chinese. Switch it live in Settings or on the first step of the setup wizard — no reload. App-written messages, including backend errors, are translated; raw `git` output is passed through as-is. Tama's にゃ〜 becomes 다옹.

English stays the source of truth and everything falls back to it, so a partial translation is still useful and adding a language never requires a complete set. See CONTRIBUTING.md if you'd like to add yours.

## Image and PDF diffs

A changed binary file is no longer just "Binary files differ". Images and PDFs now get a real side-by-side before/after preview, with a zoom lightbox and a download button for either side, so you can check what actually changed in an asset without leaving the app or digging the blob out by hand.

PDFs are rasterized by PDFium inside the Rust core rather than in the webview. That's deliberate: rendering them in the webview froze the UI outright on macOS, so the work happens on its own thread in the backend and the interface stays responsive on a large document.

## A graph that responds better

- Clicking a branch or tag in the sidebar jumps the graph to that ref's tip commit. Checking out is now the **double**-click (or right-click, or the ⋮ button), so a single stray click can no longer change your working tree.
- Double-click the "Uncommitted changes" row to open its expanded diff directly.
- Opening a repo that's already open focuses the existing window instead of launching a second one on the same repository.
- Search and copy give you the **full** commit hash, not the abbreviated one — so a hash copied out of GitCat pastes into `git` and works.
- Ref-chip hit regions are recomputed on demand instead of rebuilt every frame, which takes measurable work out of the scroll path on ref-dense histories.

## Bisect works again on current git

git 2.55 changed the wording of `git bisect log`, quoting the term — `# first 'bad' commit:` where earlier versions wrote `# first bad commit:`. GitCat matched the old spelling, so on git 2.55 or newer it never saw that the bisect had converged: an automated `bisect run` looped without terminating, and a manual bisect kept asking you to mark good/bad after git already had the answer.

GitCat now matches the shape of that line rather than one spelling of it, so it works on both git generations and with custom terms (`--term-old`/`--term-new`). If you tried bisect recently and it seemed to hang, this was why.

## Fixes

- The pinned "Uncommitted changes" band on the canvas is translated now, rather than staying English in every locale.
- Dragging the pane divider no longer throws when no repository is open, or when the graph is empty.
- An armed jump warning is correctly superseded by a later jump, including a successful one.

## Docs and website

The homepage is rebuilt around weighted sections instead of a flat card grid, the README is about a third shorter, and the screenshots are regenerated — including a Korean one. The demo video moved into Git LFS.

## Known limitation

The type-to-confirm dialog guarding destructive operations (delete branch, force switch, reset to upstream, remove submodule, delete tag) is still English-only in every locale, because it builds its text from literals rather than translation keys. Tama warns you in your own language over an English modal. This predates Korean — Chinese users have had it since 1.1 — and it's tracked for a follow-up.

name: GitCat v1.1.0
body:
GitCat's first feature release since 1.0. It's about reach and extensibility: a full plugin system, a complete Chinese translation you can switch on the fly, opening repos straight from a terminal, and a friendlier commit graph. Every operation that touches history still snapshots first, so Undo (⌘Z) is always one keystroke away.

## Plugins

GitCat is now extensible. A plugin can add commands to the ⌘K palette, register named external diff/merge tools, hook into what's happening in the repo, contribute its own side panels, and give Tama new reactions and skins so the cat responds to your own workflow.

Anything a plugin does that mutates the repo goes through the same Safety-Manager snapshot as the rest of the app, so a misbehaving plugin can't cost you work. Authoring docs and a few example plugins ship alongside, so there's something to copy from on day one.

## Chinese (中文) language

The whole app can run in Simplified Chinese now, and you can switch language live, with no reload. Choose it in Settings, or on the opening step of the first-run setup wizard. Tama keeps her にゃ〜 either way. App-written messages, including backend errors, are translated too; raw `git` output is passed through as-is.

English stays the source of truth and everything falls back to it, so contributing a translation, or a whole new language, never requires a complete set to be useful. See CONTRIBUTING.md if you'd like to help.

## A friendlier graph and sidebar

Branch and tag labels now draw as chips right before a commit's subject, so refs sit next to the work they point at. Prefer the old separate column? There's a Settings toggle for that. Local and remote tips of the same name fold into a single chip, with a hover tooltip for the full name and a right-click menu on the label itself.

The sidebar groups branches by their `/` segments (`feature/…`, `fix/…`) into a collapsible folder tree, and changing which branches are visible now reliably refreshes the graph.

## Open from the command line

Install a `gitcat` command and open any repo from your terminal the way `code .` works in VS Code:

```
gitcat .
```

It works on macOS, Linux, and Windows, returns your terminal immediately instead of blocking, and reaches into WSL too. Install it from Settings, from ⌘K, or as an optional step in the setup wizard.

## Docs

A new user manual (Guide) walks through the core workflows.

## Fixes and under the hood

- Branch-visibility changes that never reached the graph, and a submodule-navigator crash on an empty repo, are both fixed.
- On Windows, `gitcat .` no longer trips over an extended-length `\\?\` path.
- CI now builds on Windows, runs the Playwright end-to-end suite, uses least-privilege workflow permissions, and keeps line endings normalized to LF. A CodeQL finding in the new i18n layer was hardened away.

name: GitCat v1.0.0
body:
GitCat is a cozy, safety-first desktop Git client (Tauri 2 + Rust + Svelte 5). This is the first stable release: leaving the 0.9.x beta line behind.

The idea behind it is simple. Every operation that touches your history should be reversible. A **Safety Manager** snapshots your repo before every mutation, so a global Undo (⌘Z) is always one keystroke away, and Undo is itself undoable.

## Highlights

- **Safety first.** Snapshot before every mutation, global Undo that's itself undoable, reflog rescue, and fsck-based recovery of dangling commits no branch or reflog points to anymore. Genuinely irreversible actions (force push, hard discard, filter-repo) are gated behind a typed danger-confirm.
- **A fast commit graph.** git2 reads plus a hand-tuned Rust swimlane layout, streamed onto a virtualized canvas. No hard cap on history depth, newest commits paint almost instantly, and scrolling stays smooth with readable text even on a 150k-commit repo.
- **The whole everyday workflow.** Stage by file, hunk, or individual line; commit, discard, stash; branch and tag actions right on the graph; fetch / pull / push with an explicit merge-or-rebase choice; cherry-pick, merge, and revert, all backed by a real 3-way conflict resolver.
- **The advanced stuff, made safe.** Linear and interactive rebase (a drag-to-reorder planner before it touches your history), squash-merge, `git bisect`, submodules you can open and manage like their own repo, patch export/apply, and a `git-filter-repo` wizard with a full backup/restore net.
- **Meets you where you work.** A ⌘K command palette, vim-style navigation, per-file history and blame with rename-following, pluggable external diff/merge tools, WSL repositories, and an in-app terminal.
- **Tama.** GitCat's Safety Manager is a cat with eight expressions wired to real moments: curious while you search, thinking hard mid-rebase, alarmed right before something irreversible, celebrating once it's safely done.
- **Yours alone.** The app never connects to any AI or analytics service. AI-assisted features, if you want them, run as external commands you configure yourself.

## What's new since v0.9.8

- **Repository Summary no longer stalls first-open on large repos.** The one-time auto-summary now skips busy repos so opening stays snappy; the full summary is still available on demand from ⌘K / Tools.
- **Fixed a Linux AppImage launch crash** (`EGL_BAD_PARAMETER`) by pinning the bundled WebKitGTK to a working version.
- **Hardened the production Content-Security-Policy**, and fixed the inline-style regression that hardening caused on Windows/WebView2.
- **Nix support.** A `flake.nix` devShell for NixOS (Rust, WebKitGTK, pnpm, and friends) plus a proper package output on Linux.
- **Website and docs.** A silent product demo, an expanded guide for opening unsigned builds (including modern macOS), plus `SECURITY.md` and structured issue forms.

## Install

Grab your platform's installer from the assets below, or see the [install guide](https://zangjiucheng.github.io/GitCat/install) for the full walkthrough.

- **macOS** (Apple Silicon / Intel): `.dmg`. Unsigned, so right-click the app → **Open** the first time (on macOS Sequoia, allow it from System Settings → Privacy & Security).
- **Windows** (x64 / arm64): `.msi` or `-setup.exe`. On the SmartScreen prompt, click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **Linux** (x64 / arm64): `.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it first), `.deb`, or `.rpm`.

GitCat is an unsigned open-source build for now, so your OS will warn about an unidentified developer. Signed macOS and Windows builds are on the roadmap.

---

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.9.8...v1.0.0

name: GitCat v0.9.8
body:
## Highlights

A submodule-navigation overhaul: move freely between a superproject and its submodules — up, down, or sideways to a sibling — from a new strip under the topbar, and switch back to a repo you were just on instantly.

### ✨ Features
- **Submodule navigator strip.** A slim bar under the topbar shows a breadcrumb of where you are (`root › child › …`, each crumb a click to jump to that ancestor) plus the current level's siblings as one-click tabs, each with a status dot. A 🌳 button opens a popover with the full recursive submodule tree — every submodule at every depth — so you can jump straight to any of them. Reaching a sibling no longer means going all the way back and re-opening it.
- **Auto-detect on open.** Opening a repo now works out where it sits in any submodule hierarchy: open a submodule folder directly (picker / dashboard / deep-link) and its parent and siblings show up automatically, the same as if you'd navigated into it in-app. The nav state refreshes on every switch, and the same submodule registered at two different paths is handled as two distinct instances with their own refs.
- **Instant switch-back (warm-graph cache).** The last few fully-loaded repo graphs are kept in memory, so bouncing between a superproject and its submodules (or between siblings) restores the graph instantly — at the same scroll position — instead of re-streaming the whole history each time. A deliberate memory-for-speed trade; it reconciles in the background so a repo changed while you were away still updates.

### 🐛 Fixes & polish
- **Removed the old "← Back to <parent>" topbar button.** The new breadcrumb jumps to any ancestor in one click, so the one-level-back button was redundant.

Two ways to tidy up this release: **reorder a commit's crowded labels** in the graph so a hidden branch or tag can be brought into view, and **discard uncommitted changes** — one file or the whole tree — always recoverably.

### ✨ Features
- **Reorder crowded commit labels.** When a commit has more branches/tags than fit the gutter, the extras used to just vanish and you were stuck with whatever came first. - **Discard uncommitted changes.** A new **"Discard all"** button in the Unstaged header clears the whole working tree (staged, unstaged, and untracked) — but recoverably: it's saved to a stash you can restore if it was a mistake. name: GitCat v0.9.4
body:
## Highlights

A stability release fixing two bugs that could make GitCat feel broken: a **UI freeze on opening a repository**, and **Undo silently doing nothing** when you have uncommitted changes.

### 🐛 Fixes
- **The UI no longer freezes when opening a repository.** The incremental graph load streamed each batch of commits with a global Tauri event, emitted from a background thread — which holds an internal webview lock while waiting on the main thread. If the main thread was simultaneously handling one of the several IPC calls a repo-open fires (dashboard status, snapshots, watcher, bisect state), the two waited on each other forever and the whole window hung. The graph now streams over a dedicated `ipc::Channel` that doesn't take that lock, so it can't deadlock this way. (This one was pinned down by 0.9.3's new crash log plus a live stack sample.)
- **Undo no longer silently does nothing when the working tree is dirty.** With uncommitted changes, Undo can't run (it resets the working tree), so it offered to stash → undo → put your changes back — but that prompt used a synchronous `window.confirm()`, which in the packaged app can return "no" without ever showing a dialog when the UI thread is busy. So Undo just appeared dead: no dialog, no message. It now uses a reliable native dialog, and always shows a message if you decline, so it can never be silent again.

name: GitCat v0.9.3
body:
## Highlights

Mostly a Windows/WSL-hardening release, plus **cherry-pick a merge commit**. On WSL repos, working-tree operations now run the distro's own git so they stop churning line endings and file permissions; a slow **fetch/pull shows a live progress modal**; and release builds finally keep a log so a crash can actually be diagnosed.

### ✨ Features
- **Cherry-pick a merge commit.** Dragging a merge onto another commit (or right-clicking it) used to be rejected — git refuses a merge without `-m`, since a merge has two parents and it needs to know which side's changes to bring in. Now GitCat opens a small chooser: pick which parent is the mainline (parent 1 = the branch merged into, the usual choice; parent 2 = the branch merged in) and it runs `cherry-pick -m <n>`. It's on both the drag gesture and the right-click **Cherry-pick onto HEAD** menu — handy when the commit and HEAD are too far apart on the graph to drag between.
- **Live progress for fetch and pull.** A slow sync — a large remote, or a WSL repo where every git call crosses the wsl.exe boundary — used to show only a disabled "Fetching…" button. Now a modal streams git's own progress ("remote: Counting objects…", "Receiving objects: 42% (…)", "Resolving deltas…") so you can see what it's doing. It's dismissable (the op keeps running), and a quick success closes itself.
- **One-click ollama default finds ollama even when it isn't on the app's PATH.** On Windows especially, ollama's installer adds `ollama.exe` to your PATH but an already-running app never sees the update. GitCat now also probes the standard install locations, so the "Use ollama default" button works without a restart. If it's found at a fixed path, the pre-filled command uses that path so it still runs after you Save.

### 🐛 Fixes
- **WSL: operations no longer churn line endings or file permissions.** Only fetch/pull/push ran through WSL's own git before; everything that writes the working tree (checkout, reset, discard, stage, stash, Undo, merge, cherry-pick, revert, bisect, `git am`) ran Windows git against the `\\wsl.localhost\` share. With the common Windows `core.autocrlf=true`, that rewrote the whole tree as CRLF (every file showing as changed) and dropped Unix executable bits (scripts becoming "permission denied" on Linux). Those operations now run the distro's own git, so line endings and modes are handled natively. (Interactive `rebase -i` on WSL is the one piece still to come.)
- **`Ctrl+O` opens the repositories dashboard on Windows.** WebView2 was swallowing the shortcut before the menu could fire; a frontend fallback now opens it, matching `⌘O` on macOS.
- **Release builds keep a crash log.** A shipped build previously kept no logs and had no panic hook, so a crash left nothing to diagnose. Now a Rust panic is logged (`PANIC at file:line`) and release builds write a small, size-capped log to your app log directory.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.9.2...v0.9.3

## Highlights

A batch of workflow touches on top of 0.9.1: **stage or unstage a whole folder at once**, a **Select all / Deselect all** toggle for per-line staging, a **force-push** option from the branch menu, a smarter **Undo** that can stash your dirty tree first, a **one-click ollama default** for commit-message generation, and a couple of Windows / refresh fixes.

### ✨ Features
- **Stage / unstage a whole folder.** The changes list groups files under their folder; each folder row now has its own Stage / Unstage buttons, so you can stage an entire directory (`src/…`) in one click instead of file by file. It scopes strictly to that folder's contents and leaves sibling root files untouched.
- **Select all / Deselect all for per-line staging.** The per-line diff bar used to appear only after you'd already checked a line, so there was no way to grab every hunk at once or clear a selection short of unchecking each box. A **Select all** toggle now shows whenever the open diff has any changed rows, flipping to **Deselect all** once anything is selected.
- **Force push, with a warning.** The branch right-click menu now offers a force push for the current branch. It spells out that it rewrites the remote history and can drop others' commits, and asks you to confirm before it runs.
- **Undo can stash a dirty tree first.** A plain Undo refuses to run when you have uncommitted changes, which made it feel broken mid-work. When the working tree is dirty, Undo now offers to **stash → undo → pop**, so it can rewind the history and re-apply your in-progress changes on top instead of turning you away.
- **One-click ollama default for commit messages.** If you have ollama installed, External Tools can fill in a working `git diff --staged | ollama run …` command for message generation with one click. It only prefills the field — you review it and Save — so GitCat still never runs anything you didn't configure yourself. You can edit or replace it freely.
- **A submodule row is badged in the changes list.** A dirty submodule shows a small `submodule` tag so it's obvious at a glance that the change is a submodule pointer, not an ordinary file edit.
- **The commit message box remembers its height.** Drag the commit section taller or shorter and it stays that way next time.

### 🐛 Fixes
- **`Ctrl+,` opens Settings on Windows.** The shortcut was swallowed on Windows; it now opens Settings the same way `⌘,` does on macOS.
- **Refresh always shows an externally-created branch.** Checking out a new branch outside the app (while it was closed) could leave the branch missing from the graph even after a manual Refresh. Refresh now forces a full re-walk, so branches created behind GitCat's back always appear.

name: GitCat v0.9.0
body:
## Highlights

**GitCat 0.9.0 is the large-repo performance release.** Everyday operations no longer re-walk your whole history: switching branches, creating or deleting a branch/tag, and staging update the graph in place instead of reloading it, so a checkout on a 150k-commit repo (GitCat is developed against CPython) is immediate rather than a multi-second stall. Scrolling that same graph now stays smooth **with its text readable the whole time**, and a plain working-tree edit doesn't touch the graph at all. Plus a searchable repositories dashboard and a Focus-mode fix.

### ✨ Features & performance
- **Instant everyday operations.** `reloadGraph` now classifies each refresh and only re-walks history when the commit DAG actually changed. Checkout / switch branch, create-rename-delete branch, create/delete tag, and staging all update the graph's refs in place — no full re-walk. Anything that genuinely adds or removes commits (commit, merge, rebase, pull, fetch, reset, …) still does a full, correct reload. The classifier is conservative: whenever anything is uncertain it falls back to a full reload, so it can never show a wrong or stale commit set.
- **Smooth, readable scrolling on huge repos (scroll-blit).** Scrolling used to re-render every visible row each frame and drop the per-row text while moving. It now copies the already-rendered frame shifted by the scroll delta and only re-renders the thin newly-exposed strip, so a big graph scrolls smoothly **at full resolution with text intact**. The reduced-resolution/motion-blur path now applies only to horizontal pan and zoom.
- **A working-tree edit doesn't reload the graph.** Editing a file (or a terminal `git add`) is detected as a pure working-tree change and refreshes only the "Uncommitted changes" badge — the commit graph, unchanged, is left completely alone (not even a refs re-check).
- **Searchable repositories dashboard (`⌘O`).** The dashboard now opens on `⌘O` (the app's single "open a repository" entry point) with a search box — type to filter your tracked repos by name, path, or branch, and press Enter to open the top hit.

### 🐛 Fixes
- **Modals no longer hide in Focus mode.** With both side panels collapsed via `⌘\`, opening the expanded-diff view (double-click a commit) showed nothing — the modal was mounted inside the collapsed panel and got hidden with it. Panel-overlay modals now render over the full-width graph as they should.

### 🔧 For contributors
- **Dev logging** (via `tauri-plugin-log`, dev builds only) records the app's key lifecycle events — graph loads, each reload fast/full decision with its reason, and what triggered a refresh (file watcher vs status poll) — to the `pnpm tauri dev` terminal and the app's log file. Enable in any build with `localStorage["gitcat.debug"]="1"`.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.8.6...v0.9.0

body:
## Highlights

This release is about knowing where you are in the graph and getting to what you want. HEAD now has a clear **"you are here"** marker and a one-key jump, commits already merged into your current branch are dimmed, and the graph's own branch/tag labels are a real right-click menu for branch operations. Search reaches branches and commits that aren't checked out in the sidebar, including a new **search by author** across all history. Two load-time stability bugs are fixed.

### ✨ Features
- **Find your place: a "you are here" marker on HEAD.** The commit HEAD points at now wears an accent ring and glow plus a bar down the left edge of its row, so your current position is obvious at a glance instead of something you have to hunt for.
- **Jump to HEAD.** A crosshair button in the topbar (and `⌘⇧H`, plus entries in `⌘K` and the `?` overlay) recentres the graph on HEAD from wherever you've scrolled.
- **Merged commits are dimmed.** Every commit already reachable from your current branch (an ancestor of HEAD) is drawn dimmer, so what's still ahead of you stands out from what's already in.
- **Right-click a branch label to manage it.** The branch and tag labels on the graph are now their own menu, separate from the commit menu. Right-click a local label for branch operations, or a remote label to check it out. Right-click a commit to switch to a branch sitting on it. Hover any label to see its full name, and the labels themselves are more legible.
- **Search reaches hidden branches.** `⌘K` now finds branches (and their commits) even when the branch isn't checked in the sidebar; picking one shows it on the graph.
- **Search commits by an author.** A new `⌘K` action and search mode lists every commit by a given author across all history (`git log --author`, matched against name and email), not just whatever's loaded on screen.
- **An in-app Help page.** `⌘K ▸ Help` opens a Help panel inside GitCat covering the graph, navigation, search, and safety features, rather than sending you to a website.

### 🐛 Fixes & performance
- **No more freeze when you act mid-load.** Opening or switching to another repo while its graph was still streaming in could turn a backlog of queued redraws into a long synchronous stall. Redraws now coalesce through the animation loop and a stale stream is cancelled the moment a new one starts, so the UI stays responsive while history loads.
- **A big load no longer restarts itself.** Opening a large repo like CPython could trigger a reload partway through: GitCat's own snapshot bookkeeping writes refs under `refs/gitgui/`, and the file watcher treated those as an external change and restarted the stream. The watcher now ignores snapshot refs, so a long load runs to completion once.
- **Smoother fast scrolling.** While you're actively flinging the graph, per-row text is skipped and the reduced-resolution path kicks in on any motion, so heavy scrolls stay fluid; full detail snaps back the instant scrolling settles.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.8.5...v0.8.6

## Highlights

The commit graph gets a real **BRANCH / TAG column** and a redesigned, node-anchored branch-colour indicator, and every column is now resizable. Scrolling a big graph stays smooth even on webviews without GPU acceleration, and a stability fix ends a class of load-time freezes for good.

A colour band runs from each commit's node rightward to a solid bar beside its message — so which branch a row belongs to reads at a glance, while the message column stays clean.

- **A "still loading" indicator.** Opening a large repo streams its history in progressively; the centred "Loading…" overlay used to vanish after the first batch, leaving no cue it was still working. A prominent top-right pill with a live commit count now stays up until the whole graph has loaded.
- **Full path on hover.** Hovering a file or folder in a commit's Changes tree (inline or in the expanded diff) shows its complete path.

### 🐛 Fixes & performance
- **A load-time freeze is fixed.** Interacting with the UI while a repo's graph streamed in, or opening a large diff, could permanently hang the app and force a quit. The cause: a minified one-line file or a pathologically long commit summary did unbounded synchronous work on the WebView's main thread (which on macOS *is* the app's main thread). String lengths are now capped end to end — diff lines in the backend, syntax highlighting and the on-canvas commit labels in the frontend — so no single string can wedge the UI, no matter the repo.
- **Smoother scrolling on software-rendered webviews.** Where the canvas isn't GPU-composited, drawing is fill-rate bound and a large graph could drop well below 60 fps. GitCat now renders at reduced resolution while you scroll (a quarter of the pixels on a HiDPI display) and snaps back to full sharpness the instant scrolling settles, with a subtle motion-blur trail so the transient softness reads as intentional. GPU builds are unaffected — this is a floor for the environments that need it.

name: GitCat v0.8.3
body:
## Highlights

A more trustworthy **conflict resolver**: it now tells you *why* a “Continue & commit” didn’t land instead of silently doing nothing, resumes a conflict left in progress, and stops a resolved-to-“ours” cherry-pick from vanishing. Plus a reworked, click-to-preview **Snapshots** ribbon with configurable auto-cleanup, and opening another repo now spawns a **real second instance** — keyboard and all.

### ✨ Features
- **Open another repo as a real separate window** — on macOS, opening a second repository now launches a genuine new instance (via LaunchServices `open -n`), like VS Code, so its keyboard (vim-nav, ⌘K) works immediately instead of only the mouse responding.
- **Resume an in-progress conflict in-app** — a cherry-pick / merge / rebase left mid-conflict (by a prior session, or started on the command line) is now surfaced in the resolver with Continue / Abort, instead of dead-ending at “a cherry-pick is already in progress — resolve or abort it first.”
- **Configurable snapshot auto-cleanup** — Settings now offers **off / by count / by age / hybrid** retention for Safety-Manager snapshots, always keeping the newest so Undo stays protected.
- **Preview any snapshot** — click a ribbon tick or a sidebar row to select that commit in the graph and see its subject, sha, age, and file list.
- **Enter opens the diff** — pressing Enter on the selected commit opens its diff view, the keyboard twin of double-click.
- **Errors stay visible over modals** — Tama’s warnings and results now also appear as a top-right toast, so they’re readable even when a modal covers her nook.

### 🐛 Fixes — conflict resolver
- **“Continue & commit” no longer silently does nothing.** When git can’t create the commit — a failing pre-commit/commit-msg hook, or a gpg-sign failure with no interactive pinentry — the resolver now pins git’s actual reason in a persistent in-modal banner, instead of re-rendering “all resolved” with a warning you’d miss.
- **A cherry-pick resolved back to “ours” no longer vanishes.** Keeping your own side for every conflict makes the pick empty; instead of silently auto-aborting with a misleading “already applied,” the resolver explains that the resolution left no change versus the current branch — and how to redo it taking “theirs” to keep the picked change.
- **Empty file-list box hidden** — the resolver’s left panel no longer renders as an empty bordered box when there are no conflicted files.
- **“No external merge tool configured” reframed** — now a calm hint pointing at the built-in Take-ours / Take-theirs + per-hunk editor (which needs no external tool at all), rather than a red failure.

### 🎞️ Snapshots ribbon
- Reworked to **plain even spacing** — older snapshots no longer cluster and pile off the bottom (which could also crash), and the tick-placement math is hardened.
- **Bigger, easier-to-click ticks.**

## Highlights

- **Diff view can now pop out full-page** — an expand button on any commit's diff opens it in a near-fullscreen view with its own file list, so a real changeset isn't stuck reading through a cramped, 320px-tall panel — click any file on the left to switch without closing it.
- **Cherry-pick/merge drag legality is now branch-aware** — dragging a commit onto a different branch's tip used to get wrongly rejected as "target is an ancestor" whenever that branch's tip happened to sit lower in the graph. It now checks real commit ancestry instead of row position, so cross-branch cherry-picks and merges — one of the most common real uses — no longer get silently blocked.
- **Sidebar: "Hide all branches"** — a one-click way to declutter a busy graph down to just the current branch, then hand-pick a few back in, next to the existing "Show all branches".

## Also in this release

- Live refresh now has a polling backup alongside the file watcher (plus a visible warning if the watcher itself fails to start), so a change made outside GitCat still shows up even if the OS-level watch doesn't fire.
- The recent-repos dashboard, and a commit's tag/branch/remote labels, now sort in a sensible priority order (most-recently-opened; tag → head → branch → remote) instead of raw file/iteration order.
- README and docs updated to cover the above, plus a proper introduction to Tama.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.7.2...v0.7.3

name: GitCat v0.7.2
body:
## Highlights

- **WSL repos now use the distro's own git** — fetch/pull/push (and force-push, tags, submodules) on a repo living inside WSL used to shell out to Windows' own git, resolving the wrong SSH keys/credentials and sometimes hanging on an unanswerable prompt. These now route through the distro itself, so credentials resolve correctly and a failed prompt fails fast instead of hanging.
- **Three overlap/layout bugs fixed** — a long tag label on a commit row no longer overlaps the author/sha columns; the Blame/History/diff icon buttons in the file list are now properly centered instead of sitting a few pixels off; and the diff panel's line-number/marker columns now stay pinned in place while you scroll right to read a long line, instead of scrolling away with it.
- **Collapsible sidebar/detail panels** — dragging a resize handle past its old minimum now keeps shrinking the panel down to a slim rail instead of just stopping there, and releasing past the halfway point snaps it fully collapsed. Click the rail (or Tab to it and press Enter/Space) to bring the panel back to whatever width it had before.

## Also in this release

- Search Code's "search at a commit" field now accepts a branch name, `HEAD`, or `HEAD~2`, not just a full SHA.
- A small "DEV" badge appears in the topbar for `tauri dev` builds only, so a dev window is easy to tell apart from a packaged build running alongside it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.7.1...v0.7.2

name: GitCat v0.7.1
body:
## Highlights

- **Streaming commit-graph loading** — no more 50,000-commit cap. Repos of any size now load incrementally, with the newest commits showing up almost instantly instead of waiting on the whole history.
- **Redesigned conflict resolver** — Ours/Theirs comparison on top, with an always-visible, editable Result panel below for hunk-by-hunk resolution. The diff view now also uses the full window instead of a small fixed-size box.
- **Push any branch** — push a branch straight from the sidebar without switching to it first, optionally under a different name on the remote.

## Also in this release

- Absolute commit dates shown alongside the relative "X ago" time in the detail panel.
- Horizontal panning for commit graphs with extremely wide branch structures.
- Auto branch-visibility mode now also hides stale, inactive branches, not just merged ones.
- A setting to show every tag on a commit, not just the first.
- The About panel now opens automatically when the startup update check finds a new version.
- Fixed the setup wizard discarding an already-validated repository when skipping the rest of the flow.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/zangjiucheng/GitCat/compare/v0.7.0...v0.7.1
